result.rationale: refreshOAuthTokens returns fetch CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT Response (plain fetch, body URLSearchParams, unhandled json) when sharing is enabled, but HubspotCalendarService annotates the result as HubspotToken and reads hubspotRefreshToken.expires_in/access_token/refresh_token. A Response object has none of those, so expiryDate = Date.now() + expires_in*1000 yields NaN and the credential key lacks tokens. The diff clearly shows this mismatch.

judged_text: With sharing enabled the awaited value of refreshOAuthTokens is a fetch Response, not the HubspotToken the variable annotation and the following expiry math assume, so `expires_in`, `access_token` and `refresh_token` property reads all yield undefined. HubSpot token refresh under sharing persists `expiryDate: NaN` and a credential key containing no access token, leaving the credential permanently expired and every HubSpot calendar operation failing once the initial token expires.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` it does `await fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response`. In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` assigns `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then proceeds as if it received a `HubspotToken` object (i.e., expects token fields like `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `expires_in`). Under sharing mode this will instead be a `Response` object, so property reads will be `undefined` and any expiry calculation will break (e.g., yielding `NaN`), matching the finding.
